variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
var x: U32 = 10
let y: U32 = 20

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
var a: U32 = 1
var b: F64 = 2.0
var c: Bool = true
var d: String = "hello"
data_types.notes: Pony has explicit bit-width primitive types.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
var z = x + y
var b = x > y
operators.notes: Standard arithmetic, but operators are actually method calls in Pony.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
if x > 0 then
  env.out.print("pos")
else
  env.out.print("neg")
end
conditionals.notes: Conditionals are expressions and end with `end`.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
for i in Range(0, 10) do
  env.out.print(i.string())
end
for_loop.notes: For loops iterate over iterators like `Range`.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
while x < 10 do
  x = x + 1
end
while_loop.notes: While loops execute a block as long as the condition is true.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
fun add(a: U32, b: U32): U32 =>
  a + b
functions.notes: Functions return the value of their last expression.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.notes: Arrays are objects in Pony and support chaining.

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
use "collections"
var m = Map[String, U32]
m("a") = 1
maps.notes: Maps require importing the collections package.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
try
  some_partial_func()?
else
  env.out.print("Error occurred")
end
error_handling.notes: Pony uses partial functions (marked with `?`) and `try-else` blocks.

comments.title: Comments & Documentation
comments.notes: Pony uses C-style // single-line and /* */ multi-line comments.

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: Pony provides explicitly sized integer and floating-point primitives with binary and hex support.

booleans.title: Booleans & Conditions
booleans.notes: Pony uses bool / boolean types with true and false literals and logical operators (&&, ||, !).

type_casting.title: Type Casting & Conversion
type_casting.notes: Pony supports explicit type casting using cast operators or constructor functions.

strings.title: Strings & Characters
strings.notes: Pony distinguishes between single-character literals and string sequences or pointer slices.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Pony supports string interpolation or printf-style formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching & Switch
pattern_matching.notes: Pony evaluates branching conditions through switch statements, match expressions, or when constructs.

range.title: Ranges & Slicing
range.notes: Pony represents ranges with range operators (.., ..<) or standard indexed iteration boundaries.

iterators.title: Iterators & Sequences
iterators.notes: Pony implements iteration through Iterator interfaces, generators, or range-for loops.

oop_classes.title: Classes & OOP
oop_classes.notes: Pony models object orientation through classes with constructors/encapsulation or structs with associated methods.

lists.title: Dynamic Arrays & Lists
lists.notes: Pony manages growable dynamic collections using vectors, ArrayLists, or dynamically reallocated heap buffers.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Pony represents heterogeneous records through tuples, structured bindings, or lightweight record structs.

sets.title: Sets & Unique Collections
sets.notes: Pony provides unique collection hashing structures with O(1) average lookup and insertion time.

modules_import.title: Modules, Packages & Imports
modules_import.notes: Pony structures namespaces and external libraries via include directives, package declarations, or module imports.
